method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, exact formula and macro replay, and case-by-case replay of the diagonal halting proof. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The two-argument halting function, normal-form indexing and the diagonal contradiction.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The halting problem asks whether a numbered computation on an input stops. The normal form supplies a partial recursive function for each natural code e and indexes every partial recursive function. The total characteristic function h returns one exactly when that computation is defined, and h cannot be partial recursive.
samples.checks: The two arguments, output values, definedness polarity, and theorem conclusion are preserved. OLCMP-012 removes the impossible no-index exception from prose.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Assuming h partial recursive, define d(y) as one when h(y,y)=0 and undefined otherwise. An index e_d for d yields contradictions in both h(e_d,e_d)=1 and h(e_d,e_d)=0 cases, so h is not partial recursive.
samples.checks: The never-satisfied x-not-equal-x mu term, both definedness equivalences and both diagonal cases are checked against the source formulas; the prose no-index branch is removed under OLCMP-012.

source_observations: OLCMP-012 documents that the preceding T/U normal form gives every natural e a partial recursive function, so the frozen no-index branches cannot arise.
limitations: The Marathi halting title is definition-controlled; no checked native source independently attests that full computability term.
